summary: APAC egress multipath mismatch causing repeated TLS retries and elevated inference p99
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC, several NimbleDocs customers reported large spikes in token-generation latency (p95 -> p99) and occasional request timeouts when targeting models served from APAC capacity. Impact: real user-facing slowdowns for inference requests, increased client retries, and token-level billing spikes due to repeated attempts.

Initial detection: NimbleDocs support flagged elevated p99 on their API token traced to requests routed to our ap-southeast-1 edge. Observability dashboards showed increased downstream TLS errors and a spike in connection reset/retry counters on the egress proxy fleet.

Why this matters: Dedicated customer serving means predictable latency is expected; these spikes violated SLOs and drove customer impact for a paying dedicated tenant.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From a client in APAC, send a text generation request to the Redwood endpoint using NimbleDocs API key, region route ap-southeast-1.
2) Observe p95/p99 token latency markedly above baseline (~500ms -> 2.5s p99 for short prompts).
3) Re-run with tcpdump on the egress proxy to capture handshake and retransmission behaviour.
4) Compare traces to a control run from eu-west where times remain normal.
logs: 2026-03-12T03:41:12Z egress-proxy[eg-37]: TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: handshake did not complete (retry count=2)
2026-03-12T03:41:13Z serving-runtime[sv-11]: request id=8f3a delayed: waiting for upstream connection; attempt=3
pcap excerpt: multiple duplicate SYNs and duplicated ACKs observed on egress interface; path MTU differences suspected
investigation_notes: 03/12 04:10 UTC - Support: validated customer traces and sample request IDs; confirmed p99 spike correlated with TLS handshake failures on egress tier.
03/12 05:00 UTC - SRE: pulled packet captures on edge egress hosts; observed asymmetric routing and repeated retransmits toward peer AS in ap-southeast-1 peering fabric.

03/12 05:30 UTC - SRE hypothesis: recent peering table update at cloud provider caused multipath selection to prefer a path with MTU or NAT translation mismatch, causing TLS fragments to be dropped and handshake retries to increase latency.

03/12 06:10 UTC - Engineering: verified that keepalive/connection-reuse remained enabled but successive TLS retries were forcing new TCP handshakes which serialized token generation on per-connection concurrency limit.
03/12 07:00 UTC - Temporary mitigation: traffic steering rule applied to prefer local peering (route preference) for ap-southeast-1 egress. Immediate p95/p99 improved for affected requests.

03/13 10:25 UTC - Root cause confirmed by cloud provider support: an automatic ECMP change in their fabric caused uneven path characteristics; one of the ECMP paths had an MTU/fragmentation issue introduced by an intermediary NAT appliance during a routing change window.

03/13 13:00 UTC - Deployment fix: updated egress routing policy to avoid the faulty AS path and added a fallback that prioritizes persistent connection reuse across healthy egress hosts. Kernel TCP retransmission parameters were tuned to reduce chained handshake retries.
03/14 08:40 UTC - Post-fix verification: 48h rolling window shows p99 back to baseline; no further TLS handshake anomalies observed.
comments: Sofia Alvarez (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reports intermittent 504s and high p99; provided sample request IDs and traces. Asked SRE to capture egress interface packets.

Kai Patel (SRE) 2026-03-12: Captured pcaps and confirmed repeated SYN retransmits to the same AS; escalating to cloud provider peering team. Applied temporary route preference to mitigate immediate impact.
NimbleDocs (Customer) 2026-03-12: Noted improvement after mitigation; requested ETA for permanent fix and whether there are billing credits for retries. Forwarded to billing/CS.

Cloud Provider NOC 2026-03-13: Acknowledged ECMP imbalance and misconfigured NAT appliance causing MTU issues during peering propagation window; provided timeline of the incident and changed local config.
Kai Patel (SRE) 2026-03-14: Confirmed full restoration; recommended follow-ups included egress health probe expansion and an automated rollback trigger for multipath deviations.
workarounds: 1) Customer-level: pin requests to eu-west region until the route update completed (temporary trade-off on latency).
2) Platform-level: applied route preference to avoid the problematic ECMP path and increased connection pool size to amortize handshake cost while fix was being implemented.
resolution: Permanent: Updated egress routing policy to de-preference the faulty AS path in ap-southeast-1, added automated egress path health checks that validate MTU and handshake success rates, and tuned TCP retransmission defaults to reduce handshake amplification from transient path defects.
resolution_notes: Routing config change rolled out 2026-03-13 13:00 UTC. Verified telemetry for 48 hours — p99 returned to baseline. Customer notified and billing team to review retry billing. Follow-up action items created: INT-4092 (egress-health-probes rollout) and a postmortem doc in Confluence.
